title: Exercise (C1: How many solutions?)
page: 2.1 Three Views of a Linear System
content: Let \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) and \(\b \in F^m\) , and let \(N\) be the solution set of \(\A\x = \0\) . Suppose \(F\) is infinite . Prove that \(\A\x = \b\) has either no solution, exactly one solution, or infinitely many solutions. Suppose \(F\) is finite . Prove that \(\A\x = \b\) has either no solution or exactly \(\lvert N \rvert\) solutions. Give a system over \(\nF_3\) with exactly three solutions. Hint: for (a), if \(N\) contains a non-zero vector \(\h\) , look at its multiples.

title: Exercise (C2: The right-hand sides that work)
page: 2.1 Three Views of a Linear System
content: Let \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) have columns \(\a_1, \dots, \a_n\) . Prove that the set \(C = \{ \b \in F^m : \A\x = \b \text{ is consistent} \}\) is a subspace of \(F^m\) . Deduce that if \(n < m\) , then there is some \(\b \in F^m\) for which \(\A\x = \b\) is inconsistent. For \(\A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}\) over \(\nR\) , find one such \(\b\) .

title: Theorem 2.1.1 (Consistency and the span of the columns)
page: 2.1 Three Views of a Linear System
content: Let \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) have columns \(\a_1, \dots, \a_n \in F^m\) , and let \(\b \in F^m\) . Then the system \(\A\x = \b\) is consistent if and only if \(\b \in \Span(\a_1, \dots, \a_n)\) . More precisely, \(\s = (s_1, \dots, s_n)\) is a solution exactly when \(\b = s_1\a_1 + \dots + s_n\a_n\) .

title: Theorem 2.1.3 (Structure of the solution set)
page: 2.1 Three Views of a Linear System
content: Let \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) and \(\b \in F^m\) , let \(N\) be the solution set of \(\A\x = \0\) , and suppose \(\p \in F^n\) is one solution of \(\A\x = \b\) . Then the solution set of \(\A\x = \b\) is \[ \p + N = \{ \p + \h : \h \in N \}. \]

title: Theorem 2.1.2 (Homogeneous solutions form a subspace)
page: 2.1 Three Views of a Linear System
content: Let \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) . The solution set \(N = \{ \x \in F^n : \A\x = \0 \}\) of the homogeneous system \(\A\x = \0\) is a subspace of \(F^n\) .

title: Corollary 2.2.5 (More unknowns than equations)
content: Let \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) with \(n > m\) . The homogeneous system \(\A\x = \0\) has a non-trivial solution. Consequently, every list of \(n\) vectors in \(F^m\) with \(n > m\) is linearly dependent.

title: Definition 2.2.1 (Elementary row operations)
content:
Let \(F\) be a field and let \(\M \in M_{m 	imes k}(F)\) have rows \(_1, \dots, _m\) . An elementary row operation on \(\M\) is one of the following. Swap two rows: for \(i 
eq j\) , exchange \(_i\) and \(_j\) . Notation: \(R_i \leftrightarrow R_j\) . Scale a row: for an index \(i\) and a scalar \(c \in F\) with \(c 
eq 0\) , replace \(_i\) by \(c_i\) . Notation: \(R_i 	o cR_i\) . Replace a row by adding a multiple of another row: for indices \(i 
eq j\) and any \(c \in F\) , replace \(_i\) by \(_i + c_j\) . Notation: \(R_i 	o R_i + cR_j\) . In each case the rows not mentioned are left unchanged.

title: Definition 2.2.4 (Reduced row echelon form)
content: A matrix \(\R \in M_{m \times k}(F)\) is in reduced row echelon form ( RREF ) if it is in row echelon form, with pivot columns \(j_1 < \dots < j_r\) , and moreover: every pivot equals \(1\) : \(r_{i j_i} = 1\) for \(i = 1, \dots, r\) ; and every pivot is the only non-zero entry in its column: \(r_{h j_i} = 0\) for all \(h \neq i\) .

title: Definition 2.2.3 (Row echelon form)
content: A matrix \(\R \in M_{m \times k}(F)\) is in row echelon form if: there is an integer \(r\) with \(0 \le r \le m\) such that rows \(1, \dots, r\) are non-zero and rows \(r + 1, \dots, m\) are zero; and if the leading entry of row \(i\) lies in column \(j_i\) , for \(i = 1, \dots, r\) , then \(j_1 < j_2 < \dots < j_r\) , strictly . The leading entries of rows \(1, \dots, r\) are the pivots of \(\R\) , and the columns \(j_1, \dots, j_r\) are its pivot columns .

title: Definition 2.2.2 (Row equivalence)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_{m \times k}(F)\) . We say \(\A\) is row equivalent to \(\B\) if \(\B\) can be obtained from \(\A\) by a finite sequence of elementary row operations. The empty sequence is allowed, so every matrix is row equivalent to itself.

title: Example (Echelon or not?)
content: Decide which of the following real matrices are in row echelon form, and which are in reduced row echelon form. Give the pivot columns where they exist. \[ \P = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}, \quad \Q = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 5 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3 \end{pmatrix}, \quad \T = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}, \quad \Z = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}. \]

title: Example (Elimination over \nF_2)
content: Solve the following system over \(\nF_2\) : \[ x_1 + x_2 + x_4 = 1, \qquad x_2 + x_3 + x_4 = 0, \qquad x_1 + x_3 + x_4 = 1 . \] How many solutions are there? What changes if the same equations are read over \(\nR\) ?

title: Example (Gauss–Jordan on a 3 \times 4 system)
content: Solve the following system over \(\nR\) by Gauss–Jordan elimination, naming each operation: \[ \begin{aligned} 2x_2 - 2x_3 + x_4 &= 3, \\ x_1 + x_2 + x_3 \phantom{{} + x_4} &= 3, \\ 2x_1 + x_2 + 3x_3 + x_4 &= 3 . \end{aligned} \]

title: Example (A system with a parameter)
content: For which \(k \in \nR\) does the system \(x + ky = 1\) , \(kx + y = 1\) have no solution, exactly one solution, or infinitely many? Find the solutions when they exist.

title: Exercise (A1)
content: List the three types of elementary row operation, including the conditions on the scalar and on the indices. Determine whether the following statement is true: “every matrix in row echelon form is in reduced row echelon form.” Justify your answer. Determine whether the following statement is true: “if the RREF of \([\, \A \mid \b \,]\) has a zero row, then \(\A\x = \b\) is inconsistent.” Justify your answer. Determine whether the following statement is true: “a homogeneous system of 3 equations in 5 unknowns over \(\nR\) has infinitely many solutions.” Justify your answer. Explain why swapping two columns of \(\A\) in \([\, \A \mid \b \,]\) is not a safe step when solving \(\A\x = \b\) .

title: Exercise (B1: Reduce and solve)
content: Reduce the augmented matrix of each system over \(\nR\) to reduced row echelon form, naming each operation. Hence decide whether the system is consistent, and if so, describe all solutions. \(x_1 + 2x_2 - x_3 = 1\) , \(2x_1 + 5x_2 + x_3 = 4\) , \(x_1 + 3x_2 + 2x_3 = 4\) . \(x_1 + x_2 + 2x_3 = 3\) , \(2x_1 + 3x_2 + 5x_3 = 7\) , \(x_1 + 2x_2 + 4x_3 = 5\) . \(x_1 - x_2 + 2x_3 + x_4 = 2\) , \(2x_1 - 2x_2 + 5x_3 + 4x_4 = 5\) , \(-x_1 + x_2 - x_3 + x_4 = -1\) .

title: Exercise (B2: A parameter)
content: For which \(k \in \nR\) is the system \[ x + y - z = 2, \qquad x + 2y + z = 3, \qquad x + y + (k^2 - 5)z = k \] inconsistent, which give exactly one solution, and which give infinitely many? Justify your answer, and find the solutions when they exist.

title: Exercise (B3: Over \nF_3)
content: Solve each system over \(\nF_3\) by reducing to RREF, naming each operation, and list all solutions. \(x + 2y + z = 1\) , \(2x + y + z = 0\) , \(x + z = 2\) . \(x + y + 2z = 1\) , \(2x + z = 2\) .

title: Exercise (C1: Why i \neq j?)
content: Consider the move “ \(R_i \to R_i + cR_i\) ”, which the definition does not allow. Show that for \(c = -1\) this move is not reversible: give a matrix on which its effect cannot be undone by any sequence of elementary row operations and moves of this kind, and a system whose solution set it changes. Show that for \(c \neq -1\) the move is an elementary row operation of another type. Explain why the condition \(i \neq j\) in type (3) therefore loses nothing.

title: Exercise (C2: The cost of elimination)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) and \(\b \in F^n\) , and suppose that Gauss–Jordan elimination on \([\, \A \mid \b \,]\) finds, for each \(l = 1, \dots, n\) , a non-zero entry in position \((l, l)\) and so never swaps. Count as one operation each multiplication or division of two scalars, under these conventions: scaling row \(l\) costs one division for each entry in columns \(l + 1, \dots, n + 1\) (the pivot is simply set to \(1\) ), and each replacement \(R_g \to R_g - cR_l\) costs one multiplication for each entry in columns \(l + 1, \dots, n + 1\) (the entry in column \(l\) is simply set to \(0\) ). Show that processing column \(l\) costs at most \(n(n + 1 - l)\) operations. Hence show that the whole elimination costs at most \(\tfrac12 (n^3 + n^2)\) operations. Roughly how many times more work is a system of \(2n\) equations than one of \(n\) equations, for large \(n\) ?

title: Exercise (C3: Solvable for every right-hand side)
content: Let \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) , and suppose that \(\A\x = \b\) is consistent for every \(\b \in F^m\) . Prove that \(m \le n\) . Hint: suppose \(m > n\) , reduce \(\A\) to its RREF \(\R\) , and run the operations backwards on \([\, \R \mid \e_m \,]\) .

title: Lemma 2.2.1 (Row operations act column by column)
content: Let \(\M = [\, \M_1 \mid \M_2 \,] \in M_{m \times k}(F)\) be split into its first \(k_1\) columns \(\M_1\) and its remaining columns \(\M_2\) . If an elementary row operation turns \(\M\) into \(\M' = [\, \M'_1 \mid \M'_2 \,]\) (split in the same place), then the same operation turns \(\M_1\) into \(\M'_1\) and \(\M_2\) into \(\M'_2\) . In particular, an elementary row operation turns a zero column into a zero column.

title: Theorem 2.2.4 (Reading solutions from the RREF)
content: Let \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) and \(\b \in F^m\) , and suppose \([\, \A \mid \b \,]\) is row equivalent to a matrix \([\, \R \mid \c \,]\) in reduced row echelon form. Let \(r_{il}\) be the entries of \(\R\) and \(\c = (c_1, \dots, c_m)\) . \(\A\x = \b\) is inconsistent if and only if the last column, column \(n + 1\) , is a pivot column of \([\, \R \mid \c \,]\) , that is, some row of \([\, \R \mid \c \,]\) is \((0 \ \cdots \ 0 \mid 1)\) . Suppose there is no pivot in the last column. Let \(j_1 < \dots < j_r\) be the pivot columns. Then for every choice of scalars \(t_l \in F\) , one for each free variable \(x_l\) , there is exactly one solution with \(x_l = t_l\) for all free \(l\) , namely the one with \[ x_{j_i} = c_i - \sum_{l \text{ free}} r_{il}\, t_l \qquad (i = 1, \dots, r). \] In particular, setting every free variable to \(0\) gives the solution \(\p\) with \(p_{j_i} = c_i\) and all other entries \(0\) . A consistent system \(\A\x = \b\) has exactly one solution if and only if it has no free variables, that is, each of the columns \(1, \dots, n\) is a pivot column.

title: Theorem 2.2.2 (Row operations preserve solutions)
content: Let \(F\) be a field. (Reversibility) If an elementary row operation turns \(\M\) into \(\M'\) , then an elementary row operation of the same type turns \(\M'\) back into \(\M\) . Row equivalence is an equivalence relation on \(M_{m \times k}(F)\) . If \([\, \A \mid \b \,]\) and \([\, \A' \mid \b' \,]\) in \(M_{m \times (n + 1)}(F)\) are row equivalent, then the systems \(\A\x = \b\) and \(\A'\x = \b'\) have the same solution set.

title: Theorem 2.2.3 (Existence of the reduced row echelon form)
content: Let \(F\) be a field. Every matrix \(\M \in M_{m \times k}(F)\) is row equivalent to a matrix in reduced row echelon form.

title: Corollary 2.3.5 (Pivot columns are well defined)
content: Let \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) have columns \(\a_1, \dots, \a_n\) . Define the pivot columns of \(\A\) to be the pivot columns of the RREF of \(\A\) . Column \(l\) is a pivot column of \(\A\) if and only if \(\a_l \notin \Span(\a_1, \dots, \a_{l-1})\) . If \(\E\) is any matrix in row echelon form that is row equivalent to \(\A\) , then the pivot columns of \(\E\) are the pivot columns of \(\A\) . In particular, every row echelon form of \(\A\) has the same number of non-zero rows.

title: Example (Two echelon forms, one reduced form)
content: Let \(\A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 1 & 3 \\ 2 & 4 & 0 & 2 \\ 3 & 6 & 2 & 7 \end{pmatrix}\) over \(\nR\) . Reduce \(\A\) to a row echelon form in two ways: first using row 1 as the first pivot row, then starting with \(R_1 \leftrightarrow R_2\) . Continue both to reduced row echelon form. Read the column relations of \(\A\) off the RREF.

title: Exercise (A1)
content: State the uniqueness theorem for the reduced row echelon form. Determine whether the following statement is true: “if \(\A\) and \(\B\) are row equivalent, then the columns of \(\A\) and the columns of \(\B\) span the same subspace.” Justify your answer. Determine whether the following statement is true: “if \(\A\) and \(\B\) are row equivalent and \(\a_3 = \a_1 - \a_2\) for the columns of \(\A\) , then \(\b_3 = \b_1 - \b_2\) for the columns of \(\B\) .” Justify your answer. Determine whether the following statement is true: “any two row echelon forms of the same matrix have the same number of zero rows.” Justify your answer. In the RREF of a matrix, what do the entries of a non-pivot column tell you about the original matrix?

title: Exercise (B1: Column relations)
content: Let \(\A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & -2 & 1 & 7 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 & 5 & 1 \end{pmatrix}\) over \(\nR\) . Find the RREF of \(\A\) , naming each operation. Hence find the pivot columns of \(\A\) , and express each non-pivot column of \(\A\) as a linear combination of the pivot columns before it. Check your answer on the columns of \(\A\) .

title: Exercise (B2: Row equivalence via the RREF)
content: Prove that two matrices \(\A, \B \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) are row equivalent if and only if they have the same RREF.

title: Exercise (B3: Row equivalent or not?)
content: Determine whether the matrices in each pair are row equivalent over \(\nR\) . Justify your answer. \(\P = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 2 & 5 & 7 \end{pmatrix}\) and \(\Q = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 & 7 \end{pmatrix}\) . \(\P = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \end{pmatrix}\) and \(\Q = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \end{pmatrix}\) .

title: Exercise (C1: Counting reduced forms)
content: List, by pivot columns, all \(2 \times 3\) matrices over \(\nF_2\) in reduced row echelon form, and show that there are exactly \(15\) of them. Deduce that \(M_{2 \times 3}(\nF_2)\) , which has \(64\) elements, splits into exactly \(15\) classes of row equivalent matrices. Show that over a field with \(q\) elements there are exactly \(2q^2 + 2q + 3\) such matrices.

title: Exercise (C2: Deleting a column)
content: Let \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) with \(n \ge 2\) , and let \(\R\) be its RREF. Let \(\A'\) and \(\R'\) be obtained from \(\A\) and \(\R\) by deleting the last column. Prove that \(\R'\) is the RREF of \(\A'\) . Show by an example that the corresponding statement for deleting the first column is false.

title: Lemma 2.3.1 (Row equivalent matrices have the same homogeneous solutions)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) be row equivalent. Then for every \(\x \in F^n\) , \(\A\x = \0\) if and only if \(\B\x = \0\) .

title: Lemma 2.3.2 (Row operations preserve column relations)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) have columns \(\a_1, \dots, \a_n\) and \(\b_1, \dots, \b_n\) , and suppose that \(\A\x = \0 \Leftrightarrow \B\x = \0\) for every \(\x \in F^n\) . This holds, for instance, if \(\A\) and \(\B\) are row equivalent ( @lem-row-equivalent-same-null-space ). Then: for all \(x_1, \dots, x_n \in F\) : \(x_1\a_1 + \dots + x_n\a_n = \0\) if and only if \(x_1\b_1 + \dots + x_n\b_n = \0\) ; for every index \(l\) and all scalars \(d_1, \dots, d_{l-1}\) : \(\a_l = d_1\a_1 + \dots + d_{l-1}\a_{l-1}\) if and only if \(\b_l = d_1\b_1 + \dots + d_{l-1}\b_{l-1}\) ; for every index \(l\) : \(\a_l \in \Span(\a_1, \dots, \a_{l-1})\) if and only if \(\b_l \in \Span(\b_1, \dots, \b_{l-1})\) .

title: Lemma 2.3.3 (Columns of a matrix in RREF)
content: Let \(\R \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) be in reduced row echelon form, with entries \(r_{il}\) , columns \(\u_1, \dots, \u_n\) , and pivot columns \(j_1 < \dots < j_r\) . For each \(i = 1, \dots, r\) , the pivot column \(\u_{j_i}\) is \(\e_i\) . If \(l\) is not a pivot column, then \[ \u_l = \sum_{i \,:\, j_i < l} r_{il}\, \e_i = \sum_{i \,:\, j_i < l} r_{il}\, \u_{j_i} . \] Column \(l\) is a pivot column if and only if \(\u_l \notin \Span(\u_1, \dots, \u_{l-1})\) .

title: Theorem 2.3.4 (Uniqueness of the reduced row echelon form)
content: Let \(\R, \R' \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) be in reduced row echelon form, and suppose that \(\R\x = \0 \Leftrightarrow \R'\x = \0\) for every \(\x \in F^n\) . Then \(\R = \R'\) . Consequently, every matrix \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) is row equivalent to exactly one matrix in reduced row echelon form, called the RREF of \(\A\) .

title: Definition 2.4.1 (Elementary matrix)
content:
Let \(m \ge 1\) . A matrix \(\E \in M_m(F)\) is an elementary matrix if it is obtained from \(\I_m\) by performing exactly one elementary row operation. Writing \(\E_{ij}\) for the matrix unit ( \(1\) in entry \((i, j)\) , \(0\) elsewhere; see @exm-standard-bases ), the three kinds are: \(\P_{ij}\) , obtained by \(R_i \leftrightarrow R_j\) with \(i 
eq j\) : the identity with rows \(i\) and \(j\) swapped; \(\D_i(c) = \diag(1, \dots, 1, c, 1, \dots, 1)\) , with \(c\) in position \(i\) , obtained by \(R_i 	o cR_i\) with \(c 
eq 0\) ; \(\I_m + c\E_{ij}\) , obtained by \(R_i 	o R_i + cR_j\) with \(i 
eq j\) and \(c \in F\) : the identity with an extra \(c\) in entry \((i, j)\) .

title: Example (Three operations, three products)
content: Let \(\A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 3 & 4 \end{pmatrix} \in M_{3 \times 2}(\nR)\) . Compute \(\P_{13}\A\) , \(\D_2(5)\A\) and \((\I_3 - 3\E_{31})\A\) , and check that each is the result of the corresponding row operation.

title: Example (A 3 \times 3 inverse)
content: Find the inverse of \(\A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 5 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & 3 \end{pmatrix} \in M_3(\nR)\) , or show that it does not exist.

title: Example (When the algorithm stops)
content: Decide whether \(\A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 2 & 5 & 7 \\ 1 & 3 & 4 \end{pmatrix} \in M_3(\nR)\) is invertible.

title: Example (Factoring into elementary matrices)
content: Write \(\A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 5 & 3 \end{pmatrix} \in M_2(\nR)\) as a product of elementary matrices, and read off \(\A^{-1}\) .

title: Exercise (A1)
content: Define an elementary matrix, and write down the \(3 \times 3\) elementary matrix that performs \(R_3 \to R_3 + 7R_1\) . State four of the conditions in @thm-invertible-tfae . True or false: the product of two elementary matrices is always an elementary matrix. Justify your answer. True or false: if \(\A \in M_{2 \times 3}(F)\) , \(\B \in M_{3 \times 2}(F)\) and \(\A\B = \I_2\) , then \(\B\A = \I_3\) . Justify your answer. True or false: if \(\A \in M_n(F)\) and \(\A\x = \e_j\) has a solution for each \(j = 1, \dots, n\) , then \(\A\) is invertible. Justify your answer. Describe the method for computing the inverse of a square matrix, and how it detects a matrix that is not invertible.

title: Exercise (B1: Inverses by row reduction)
content:
For each matrix, find the inverse or show that it is not invertible. \(\A =  egin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 & 2 \ 2 & 1 & 3 \ 4 & 1 & 8 \end{pmatrix} \in M_3(
R)\) . \(\B =  egin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & -1 \ 0 & 1 & 1 \ 2 & 5 & -1 \end{pmatrix} \in M_3(
R)\) . \(\C =  egin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 & 0 \ 0 & 1 & 1 \ 1 & 1 & 1 \end{pmatrix} \in M_3(
F_2)\) .

title: Exercise (B2: A product of elementary matrices)
content: Let \(\A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 3 \\ 2 & 5 \end{pmatrix} \in M_2(\nR)\) . Write \(\A\) as a product of elementary matrices. Hence write \(\A^{-1}\) as a product of elementary matrices, and compute it.

title: Exercise (B3: Invertible products)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) , and suppose \(\A\B\) is invertible. Prove that \(\A\) and \(\B\) are both invertible.

title: Exercise (C1: Triangular matrices)
content: Let \(\U = (u_{ij}) \in M_n(F)\) be upper triangular ( @def-upper-triangular ). Prove that \(\U\) is invertible if and only if \(u_{ii} \neq 0\) for every \(i\) . Prove that if \(\U\) is invertible, then \(\U^{-1}\) is upper triangular. Hint: for (a), use item (b) or item (f) of @thm-invertible-tfae ; for (b), consider the systems \(\U\x = \e_k\) .

title: Exercise (C2: All right inverses)
content:
Let \(\A =  egin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 & 1 \ 0 & 1 & 1 \end{pmatrix} \in M_{2 	imes 3}(
R)\) . Find all \(\B \in M_{3 	imes 2}(
R)\) with \(\A\B = \I_2\) . Show that there is no \(\C \in M_{3 	imes 2}(
R)\) with \(\C\A = \I_3\) .

title: Exercise (C3: Nilpotent perturbations of the identity)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) and suppose \(\A^k = 0\) for some integer \(k \ge 1\) . Prove that \(\I_n + \A\) is invertible, by using item (b) of @thm-invertible-tfae . Verify that \((\I_n + \A)(\I_n - \A + \A^2 - \dots + (-1)^{k-1}\A^{k-1}) = \I_n\) , and deduce a formula for \((\I_n + \A)^{-1}\) .

title: Lemma 2.4.3 (Square reduced matrices)
content: Let \(\R \in M_n(F)\) be in reduced row echelon form. Then either \(\R = \I_n\) , or the last row of \(\R\) is zero.

title: Theorem 2.4.2 (Elementary matrices are invertible)
content: Every elementary matrix is invertible, and its inverse is an elementary matrix of the same kind: \[ \P_{ij}^{-1} = \P_{ij}, \qquad \D_i(c)^{-1} = \D_i(c^{-1}), \qquad (\I_m + c\E_{ij})^{-1} = \I_m - c\E_{ij} \quad (i \neq j). \]

title: Theorem 2.4.6 (Inverse by row reduction)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) , and let \([\R \mid \C]\) be the reduced row echelon form of \([\A \mid \I_n]\) , with \(\R, \C \in M_n(F)\) . Then \(\R\) is the reduced row echelon form of \(\A\) . Consequently, \(\A\) is invertible if and only if \(\R = \I_n\) , and in that case \(\A^{-1} = \C\) .

title: Theorem 2.4.4 (Invertible Matrix Theorem)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) , with columns \(\a_1, \dots, \a_n \in F^n\) . The following are equivalent. \(\A\) is invertible. The homogeneous system \(\A\x = \0\) has only the trivial solution \(\x = \0\) . The reduced row echelon form of \(\A\) is \(\I_n\) . \(\A\) is a product of elementary matrices. For every \(\b \in F^n\) , the system \(\A\x = \b\) has a solution. The columns \((\a_1, \dots, \a_n)\) are linearly independent. The columns \((\a_1, \dots, \a_n)\) span \(F^n\) . The columns \((\a_1, \dots, \a_n)\) form a basis of \(F^n\) .

title: Theorem 2.4.5 (One-sided inverses of square matrices)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) . If \(\A\B = \I_n\) , then \(\B\A = \I_n\) . Hence \(\A\) and \(\B\) are both invertible, \(\B = \A^{-1}\) and \(\A = \B^{-1}\) .

title: Theorem 2.4.7 (Row equivalence is left multiplication by an invertible matrix)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) . Then \(\A\) is row equivalent to \(\B\) (that is, \(\B\) can be reached from \(\A\) by row operations) if and only if \(\B = \E\A\) for some invertible \(\E \in M_m(F)\) .

title: Theorem 2.4.1 (Row operations are left multiplications)
content: Let \(\rho\) be an elementary row operation on matrices with \(m\) rows, and let \(\E = \rho(\I_m)\) be the corresponding elementary matrix. Then for every \(n \ge 1\) and every \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) , \[ \rho(\A) = \E\A . \]

title: Corollary 2.5.6 (Rank from any echelon form)
page: 2.5 Row Space, Column Space, Null Space and Rank
content: Let \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) , and let \(\G\) be a matrix in row echelon form that is row equivalent to \(\A\) . Then the number of non-zero rows of \(\G\) is \(\rank \A\) , and the columns of \(\G\) containing its pivots are exactly the pivot columns of \(\A\) .

title: Definition 2.5.1 (Column space)
page: 2.5 Row Space, Column Space, Null Space and Rank
content: The column space of \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) is the span of its columns, \[ \col(\A) \coloneqq \Span(\a_1, \dots, \a_n) = \{ \A\x : \x \in F^n \} \subseteq F^m . \]

title: Definition 2.5.3 (Null space)
page: 2.5 Row Space, Column Space, Null Space and Rank
content: The null space of \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) is the solution set of the homogeneous system, \[ \nul(\A) \coloneqq \{ \x \in F^n : \A\x = \0 \} \subseteq F^n . \]

title: Definition 2.5.5 (Nullity of a matrix)
page: 2.5 Row Space, Column Space, Null Space and Rank
content: The nullity of \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) is \(\nullity \A \coloneqq \dim \nul(\A)\) .

title: Definition 2.5.4 (Rank of a matrix)
page: 2.5 Row Space, Column Space, Null Space and Rank
content: The rank of \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) is \(\rank \A \coloneqq \dim \col(\A)\) .

title: Definition 2.5.2 (Row space)
page: 2.5 Row Space, Column Space, Null Space and Rank
content: The row space of \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) is the span of its rows, \[ \row(\A) \coloneqq \Span(\text{row } 1, \dots, \text{row } m) \subseteq M_{1 \times n}(F) . \]

title: Example (Bases for the running example)
page: 2.5 Row Space, Column Space, Null Space and Rank
content: Find bases of \(\col(\A)\) , \(\row(\A)\) and \(\nul(\A)\) , and the rank and nullity, for \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 0 & 0 & -1 \\ 2 & 4 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \end{pmatrix} \in M_{4 \times 5}(\nR). \]

title: Example (Counting solutions over \nF_3)
page: 2.5 Row Space, Column Space, Null Space and Rank
content: Over \(\nF_3\) , consider \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 1 & 2 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \b = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \b' = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}. \] Decide whether \(\A\x = \b\) and \(\A\x = \b'\) are consistent, and count their solutions.

title: Example (Extending to a basis by elimination)
page: 2.5 Row Space, Column Space, Null Space and Rank
content: Extend the independent list \((\v_1, \v_2) = ((1, 2, 0, 1), (2, 4, 1, 1))\) from @exm-independence-by-rank to a basis of \(\nR^4\) .

title: Example (Testing independence)
page: 2.5 Row Space, Column Space, Null Space and Rank
content: Decide whether \(\v_1 = (1, 2, 0, 1)\) , \(\v_2 = (2, 4, 1, 1)\) , \(\v_3 = (0, 0, 1, -1)\) are linearly independent in \(\nR^4\) . If not, find a linear relation.

title: Example (A basis of an intersection)
page: 2.5 Row Space, Column Space, Null Space and Rank
content: For \(U\) and \(W\) as in @exm-sum-by-elimination , find a basis of \(U \cap W\) , and check the Dimension Formula for Sums.

title: Example (A basis of a sum)
page: 2.5 Row Space, Column Space, Null Space and Rank
content: Let \(U = \Span(\u_1, \u_2)\) and \(W = \Span(\w_1, \w_2)\) in \(\nR^4\) , where \[ \u_1 = (1, 0, 1, 2), \quad \u_2 = (0, 1, 1, 1), \quad \w_1 = (1, 1, 0, 1), \quad \w_2 = (1, 3, 0, 1). \] Find a basis and the dimension of \(U + W\) .

title: Exercise (A1)
page: 2.5 Row Space, Column Space, Null Space and Rank
content: Define \(\col(\A)\) , \(\row(\A)\) , \(\nul(\A)\) and \(\rank \A\) for \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) , and say which space each subspace lives in. State the Rank–Nullity Theorem for matrices and the Rouché–Capelli Theorem. True or false: if \(\R\) is the RREF of \(\A\) , then \(\col(\R) = \col(\A)\) . Justify your answer. True or false: there is a \(4 \times 6\) real matrix with nullity \(1\) . Justify your answer. True or false: for every \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) , \(\rank \A = \rank \A\tp\) . Justify your answer. Describe how to find a basis of \(U \cap W\) for subspaces \(U, W \subseteq F^m\) given by bases.

title: Exercise (B2: Independence and extension in \nR^4)
page: 2.5 Row Space, Column Space, Null Space and Rank
content: Let \(\v_1 = (1, 0, 2, 1)\) , \(\v_2 = (2, 1, 3, 1)\) , \(\v_3 = (0, 1, -1, -1)\) in \(\nR^4\) . Determine whether \((\v_1, \v_2, \v_3)\) is linearly independent. Justify your answer. Find a basis of \(\Span(\v_1, \v_2, \v_3)\) , and extend it to a basis of \(\nR^4\) using standard basis vectors.

title: Exercise (B3: Sum and intersection in \nR^5)
page: 2.5 Row Space, Column Space, Null Space and Rank
content: Let \(U = \Span(\u_1, \u_2, \u_3)\) and \(W = \Span(\w_1, \w_2)\) in \(\nR^5\) , where \[ \begin{aligned} &\u_1 = (1, 1, 0, 0, 1), \quad \u_2 = (0, 1, 1, 0, 0), \quad \u_3 = (1, 0, 0, 1, 0), \\ &\w_1 = (1, 2, 2, 1, 2), \quad \w_2 = (0, 0, 1, 1, 1). \end{aligned} \] Find \(\dim U\) , \(\dim W\) , a basis of \(U + W\) and a basis of \(U \cap W\) . Hence verify @thm-dimension-formula-subspace-dim .

title: Exercise (C1: Rank of a sum)
page: 2.5 Row Space, Column Space, Null Space and Rank
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) . Prove that \(\rank(\A + \B) \le \rank \A + \rank \B\) . Give an example where the inequality is strict.

title: Exercise (C2: Matrices of rank one)
page: 2.5 Row Space, Column Space, Null Space and Rank
content: Let \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) . Prove that \(\rank \A = 1\) if and only if \(\A = \x\y\tp\) for some non-zero \(\x \in F^m\) and \(\y \in F^n\) .

title: Exercise (C3: The matrix i + j)
page: 2.5 Row Space, Column Space, Null Space and Rank
content: For \(n \ge 1\) , let \(\A_n \in M_n(\nR)\) have entries \(a_{ij} = i + j\) . Prove that \(\rank \A_1 = 1\) and \(\rank \A_n = 2\) for every \(n \ge 2\) . Hence find \(\nullity \A_n\) . Hint: write each row as a combination of two fixed row vectors.

Let \(F\) be a finite field with \(q\) elements, and let \(\A \in M_{m 	imes n}(F)\) have rank \(r\) . Prove that exactly \(q^{r}\) vectors \(  \in F^m\) make \(\A\x =  \) consistent. By counting the pairs \((\x,  ) \in F^n 	imes F^m\) with \(\A\x =  \) in two ways, and using @thm-general-solution-structure but not @thm-rank-nullity-matrix , prove that \(

title: Proposition 2.5.11 (Sum and intersection by elimination)
page: 2.5 Row Space, Column Space, Null Space and Rank
content:
Let \(U, W \subseteq F^m\) be subspaces with bases \((\u_1, \dots, \u_k)\) and \((\w_1, \dots, \w_l)\) , and let \(\M =  egin{pmatrix} \u_1 & \cdots & \u_k & \w_1 & \cdots & \w_l \end{pmatrix} \in M_{m 	imes (k+l)}(F)\) . Then: the pivot columns of \(\M\) form a basis of \(U + W\) ; for \(\x = (x_1, \dots, x_{k+l}) \in F^{k+l}\) write \(\u_{\x} \coloneqq x_1\u_1 + \dots + x_k\u_k\) , the combination of the \(\u\) ’s with the first \(k\) entries of \(\x\) as coefficients. If \((
_1, \dots,

ul(\M)\) , then \((\u_{

_d})\) is a basis of \(U \cap W\) . In particular \(\dim(U + W) = ank \M\) and \(\dim(U \cap W) = 
ullity \M\) .

title: Theorem 2.5.2 (Pivot columns form a basis of the column space)
page: 2.5 Row Space, Column Space, Null Space and Rank
content: Let \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) have pivot columns \(j_1 < \dots < j_r\) , and let \(\R = (r_{kj})\) be its RREF. Then: the pivot columns of \(\A\) , \((\a_{j_1}, \dots, \a_{j_r})\) , form a basis of \(\col(\A)\) ; if column \(j\) is free and \(t\) pivot columns lie to its left, then \(\a_j = r_{1j}\a_{j_1} + \dots + r_{tj}\a_{j_t}\) ; the pivot columns of \(\A\) are exactly the vectors kept when \((\a_1, \dots, \a_n)\) is sifted as in @thm-sift .

title: Theorem 2.5.4 (Basis of the null space)
page: 2.5 Row Space, Column Space, Null Space and Rank
content: Let \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) have RREF \(\R = (r_{kj})\) with pivot columns \(j_1 < \dots < j_r\) . For each free column \(f\) , define \(\s_f \in F^n\) by \[ \begin{aligned} (\s_f)_f &= 1, \\ (\s_f)_{f'} &= 0 \text{ for every other free } f', \\ (\s_f)_{j_k} &= -r_{kf} \text{ for } k = 1, \dots, r . \end{aligned} \] Then the vectors \(\s_f\) , one for each free column \(f\) , form a basis of \(\nul(\A)\) . In particular \(\nullity \A = n - r\) , the number of free columns.

title: Theorem 2.5.3 (Basis of the row space)
page: 2.5 Row Space, Column Space, Null Space and Rank
content: The non-zero rows of the RREF \(\R\) of \(\A\) form a basis of \(\row(\A)\) .

title: Theorem 2.5.10 (Independence and spanning by rank)
page: 2.5 Row Space, Column Space, Null Space and Rank
content: Let \(\v_1, \dots, \v_k \in F^m\) , and let \(\A = \begin{pmatrix} \v_1 & \cdots & \v_k \end{pmatrix} \in M_{m \times k}(F)\) . Then: \((\v_1, \dots, \v_k)\) is linearly independent if and only if \(\rank \A = k\) , that is, every column is a pivot column; \((\v_1, \dots, \v_k)\) spans \(F^m\) if and only if \(\rank \A = m\) , that is, every row of the RREF has a pivot; \((\v_1, \dots, \v_k)\) is a basis of \(F^m\) if and only if \(k = m = \rank \A\) .

title: Theorem 2.5.7 (Rank–Nullity for Matrices)
page: 2.5 Row Space, Column Space, Null Space and Rank
content: For every \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) , \[ \rank \A + \nullity \A = n, \] the number of columns of \(\A\) .

title: Theorem 2.5.9 (Rank of a product)
page: 2.5 Row Space, Column Space, Null Space and Rank
content: Let \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) and \(\B \in M_{n \times p}(F)\) . Then \[ \rank(\A\B) \le \min(\rank \A, \rank \B). \] Moreover, if \(\P \in M_m(F)\) and \(\Q \in M_n(F)\) are invertible, then \(\rank(\P\A) = \rank \A = \rank(\A\Q)\) .

title: Theorem 2.5.8 (Rouché–Capelli Theorem)
page: 2.5 Row Space, Column Space, Null Space and Rank
content: Let \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) , \(\b \in F^m\) , and let \([\A \mid \b] \in M_{m \times (n+1)}(F)\) be the augmented matrix. The system \(\A\x = \b\) is consistent if and only if \(\rank \A = \rank\,[\A \mid \b]\) . Suppose it is consistent, let \(\p\) be one solution, let \(r = \rank \A\) , and let \(\s_1, \dots, \s_{n-r}\) be a basis of \(\nul(\A)\) . Then every solution can be written as \[ \x = \p + t_1\s_1 + \dots + t_{n-r}\s_{n-r} \] for exactly one choice of \((t_1, \dots, t_{n-r}) \in F^{n-r}\) . In words: the solutions form an \((n - r)\) -parameter family. If moreover \(F\) is a finite field with \(q\) elements (for instance \(\nF_p\) , with \(q = p\) ), a consistent system has exactly \(q^{\,n - \rank \A}\) solutions.

title: Theorem 2.5.1 (Row operations and the three spaces)
page: 2.5 Row Space, Column Space, Null Space and Rank
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) be row equivalent. Then: \(\row(\B) = \row(\A)\) ; \(\nul(\B) = \nul(\A)\) . Equivalently, writing \(\b_1, \dots, \b_n\) for the columns of \(\B\) : for all \(c_1, \dots, c_n \in F\) , the columns of \(\A\) satisfy \(c_1\a_1 + \dots + c_n\a_n = \0\) if and only if the columns of \(\B\) satisfy \(c_1\b_1 + \dots + c_n\b_n = \0\) ; but \(\col(\B)\) and \(\col(\A)\) need not be equal.

title: Theorem 2.5.5 (Row rank equals column rank)
page: 2.5 Row Space, Column Space, Null Space and Rank
content: Let \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) , and let \(r\) be the number of pivots of its RREF. Then \[ \dim \row(\A) = \dim \col(\A) = r . \] Consequently \(\rank \A = \rank \A\tp\) .

title: Definition 2.6.1 (LU factorization)
content: A matrix \(\L \in M_n(F)\) is unit lower triangular if it is lower triangular and every diagonal entry equals \(1\) . Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) . An LU factorization of \(\A\) is a pair \((\L, \U)\) of matrices in \(M_n(F)\) such that \[ \A = \L\U, \qquad \L \text{ is \textbf{unit} lower triangular}, \qquad \U \text{ is upper triangular}. \]

title: Definition 2.6.2 (Permutation matrix)
content: Let \(\sigma \in S_n\) be a permutation of \(\{1, \dots, n\}\) . The permutation matrix of \(\sigma\) is \[ \P_\sigma = \begin{pmatrix} \e_{\sigma(1)} & \e_{\sigma(2)} & \cdots & \e_{\sigma(n)} \end{pmatrix} \in M_n(F), \] the matrix whose \(j\) -th column is \(\e_{\sigma(j)}\) . A matrix is a permutation matrix if it equals \(\P_\sigma\) for some \(\sigma \in S_n\) .

title: Definition 2.6.3 (PLU factorization)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) . A PLU factorization of \(\A\) is a triple \((\P, \L, \U)\) of matrices in \(M_n(F)\) such that \[ \begin{aligned} &\P\A = \L\U, \qquad \P \text{ is a permutation matrix}, \\ &\L \text{ is unit lower triangular}, \qquad \U \text{ is upper triangular}. \end{aligned} \]

title: Example (An LU factorization from elimination)
content: Let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 4 & 5 & -1 \\ -2 & 8 & 2 \end{pmatrix} \in M_3(\nQ). \] Reduce \(\A\) to upper triangular form using only operations “subtract a multiple of a higher row from a lower row”, and record each multiplier. Compare the result with the matrix \(\U\) of the previous subsection.

title: Example (Two right-hand sides, one factorization)
content: Let \(\A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 4 & 5 & -1 \\ -2 & 8 & 2 \end{pmatrix}\) with the factorization \(\A = \L\U\) of @exm-lu-by-elimination . Solve \(\A\x = \b\) for \[ \b = \begin{pmatrix} -1 \\ -3 \\ -6 \end{pmatrix} \quad\text{and}\quad \b' = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 7 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}. \]

title: Example (An invertible matrix with no LU factorization)
content: Show that \(\A = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix} \in M_2(F)\) has no LU factorization, over any field \(F\) , although \(\A\) is invertible.

title: Example (A swap in the middle)
content: Find a PLU factorization of \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 4 & 3 \\ 3 & 7 & 2 \end{pmatrix} \in M_3(\nQ). \]

title: Exercise (A1)
content: Define an LU factorization of a matrix \(\A \in M_n(F)\) , and a PLU factorization. True or false: every invertible matrix has an LU factorization. Justify your answer. Suppose \(\A = \L\U\) . In which order are the two triangular systems solved to find a solution of \(\A\x = \b\) , and what is each one? True or false: the product of two unit lower triangular \(n \times n\) matrices is unit lower triangular. Justify your answer. True or false: the zero matrix in \(M_2(F)\) has more than one LU factorization. Justify your answer. What is the inverse of a permutation matrix \(\P\) ?

title: Exercise (B1: An LU factorization)
content: Find the LU factorization of \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 0 \\ -3 & -7 & 4 \\ 2 & 6 & -3 \end{pmatrix} \in M_3(\nQ) \] by elimination without row swaps. Hence show that \(\A\) is invertible.

title: Exercise (B2: Two systems, one factorization)
content: With \(\A = \L\U\) as in @exr-lu-factorization-b1 , solve \(\A\x = \b\) for \(\b = (3, -6, 5)\) and for \(\b = (0, 1, -2)\) , using only forward and back substitution.

title: Exercise (B3: A PLU factorization)
content: Let \(\A = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 1 \end{pmatrix} \in M_3(\nQ)\) . Explain why \(\A\) has no LU factorization. Find a PLU factorization of \(\A\) . Hence solve \(\A\x = (0, 2, 7)\) .

title: Exercise (C1: Leading principal submatrices)
content: For \(\A \in M_n(F)\) and \(1 \le k \le n\) , the leading principal submatrix \(\A_k \in M_k(F)\) is the top-left \(k \times k\) corner of \(\A\) , with entries \(a_{ij}\) for \(i, j \le k\) . Let \(\L\) be lower triangular and \(\U\) upper triangular in \(M_n(F)\) . Show that \((\L\U)_k = \L_k \U_k\) for every \(k\) . Deduce that if \(\A\) has an LU factorization \(\A = \L\U\) with \(\U\) invertible, then every leading principal submatrix \(\A_1, \dots, \A_n\) is invertible. Prove the converse: if \(\A_1, \dots, \A_n\) are all invertible, then \(\A\) has an LU factorization with \(\U\) invertible. Hint for (c): induction on \(n\) . Write \(\A\) with \(\A_{n-1}\) in its top-left corner, a column \(\b\) , a row \(\c\tp\) and a corner entry \(d\) , and look for \(\L\) and \(\U\) of the same shape.

title: Exercise (C2: An LDLᵀ factorization)
content: Let \(\A = \begin{pmatrix} 4 & -4 & 8 \\ -4 & 5 & -11 \\ 8 & -11 & 27 \end{pmatrix} \in M_3(\nR)\) . Find the LU factorization of \(\A\) , show that \(\A\) is invertible, and write \(\A = \L\D\L\tp\) . Deduce that \(\x\tp \A\x > 0\) for every non-zero \(\x \in \nR^3\) .

title: Exercise (C3: Counting matrices without an LU factorization)
content: Let \(\A = \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix} \in M_2(F)\) . Prove that \(\A\) has an LU factorization if and only if \(a \neq 0\) or \(c = 0\) . Let \(q\) be a prime. How many matrices in \(M_2(\nF_q)\) have no LU factorization? List them for \(q = 2\) .

title: Lemma 2.6.3 (Multiplier matrices)
content: Let \(1 \le k \le n\) , and let \(\v, \v_1, \dots, \v_m \in F^n\) be vectors such that the first \(k\) entries of \(\v\) are zero and, for each \(j\) , the first \(j\) entries of \(\v_j\) are zero ( \(m \le n\) ). Then: \(\G_k(\v)\) is the product, in any order, of the elementary matrices \(\I + v_i \E_{ik}\) for \(i = k+1, \dots, n\) ; \(\G_k(\v) \G_k(-\v) = \G_k(-\v) \G_k(\v) = \I\) ; \(\G_1(\v_1) \G_2(\v_2) \cdots \G_m(\v_m) = \I + \v_1 \e_1\tp + \v_2 \e_2\tp + \dots + \v_m \e_m\tp\) .

title: Lemma 2.6.6 (Permutation matrices)
content: Let \(\sigma, \tau \in S_n\) . \(\P_\sigma \P_\tau = \P_{\sigma \circ \tau}\) . In particular a product of permutation matrices is a permutation matrix. \(\P_\sigma\) is invertible and \(\P_\sigma^{-1} = \P_\sigma\tp\) . If \(\tau = (r\ s)\) is a transposition, then \(\P_\tau\) is the elementary matrix \(\P_{rs}\) that swaps rows \(r\) and \(s\) , and \(\P_\tau^2 = \I\) . Let \(1 \le k < r < s \le n\) , let \(\tau = (r\ s)\) , and let \(\v \in F^n\) have its first \(k\) entries zero. Then \(\P_\tau \v\) has its first \(k\) entries zero, and \[ \P_\tau\, \G_k(\v)\, \P_\tau = \G_k(\P_\tau \v). \]

title: Lemma 2.6.2 (Invertibility of a triangular matrix)
content: An upper triangular matrix \(\U \in M_n(F)\) is invertible if and only if every diagonal entry \(u_{11}, \dots, u_{nn}\) is non-zero.

title: Lemma 2.6.1 (Unit lower triangular matrices are closed)
content: Let \(\L, \L' \in M_n(F)\) be unit lower triangular. Then: \(\L\L'\) is unit lower triangular; \(\L\) is invertible, and \(\L^{-1}\) is unit lower triangular.

title: Theorem 2.6.8 (LDLᵀ factorization)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be symmetric and invertible , and suppose \(\A = \L\U\) is an LU factorization. Then the diagonal entries \(u_{11}, \dots, u_{nn}\) of \(\U\) are non-zero, and with \(\D = \diag(u_{11}, \dots, u_{nn})\) , \[ \U = \D\L\tp \qquad\text{and}\qquad \A = \L\D\L\tp . \]

title: Theorem 2.6.4 (LU from elimination)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) , and suppose elimination without row swaps succeeds on \(\A\) , with multipliers \(\ell_{ik}\) and result \(\U\) . Let \(\L\) be the unit lower triangular matrix whose \((i, k)\) -entry is \(\ell_{ik}\) for every \(i > k\) . Then \(\U\) is upper triangular and \[ \A = \L\U . \] In particular \(\A\) has an LU factorization.

title: Theorem 2.6.5 (Uniqueness of the LU factorization)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be invertible . If \(\A = \L_1\U_1\) and \(\A = \L_2\U_2\) are LU factorizations, then \(\L_1 = \L_2\) and \(\U_1 = \U_2\) .

title: Theorem 2.6.7 (Existence of a PLU factorization)
content: Every \(\A \in M_n(F)\) has a PLU factorization.

title: Definition 2.7.1 (Incidence matrix)
content: The incidence matrix of a network with vertices \(1, \dots, m\) and edges \(1, \dots, k\) , where \(k \ge 1\) , is \(\N \in M_{m \times k}(\nR)\) with \[ \N_{ve} = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } v = \operatorname{tail}(e), \\ -1 & \text{if } v = \operatorname{head}(e), \\ 0 & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]

title: Example (Burning ammonia)
content: Find all solutions of the system above over \(\nQ\) , and hence the balanced equation with the smallest positive integer coefficients.

title: Example (A cubic through four points)
content: Find the polynomial \(p \in \nQ[x]_{\le 3}\) whose graph passes through \((-1, 2)\) , \((0, 1)\) , \((1, 2)\) and \((2, 11)\) .

title: Example (Every pattern of the 3 × 3 puzzle is solvable)
content: Show that \(\rank \A = 9\) . Deduce that every one of the \(2^9 = 512\) starting patterns can be switched off, by exactly one set of presses.

title: Example (Switching off the center)
content: Only the center light is on. Which buttons should be pressed?

title: Example (Traffic in a town center)
content: Four intersections are joined by one-way streets \(1 \to 2\) , \(2 \to 3\) , \(3 \to 4\) , \(4 \to 1\) and \(1 \to 3\) , carrying unknown flows \(f_1, \dots, f_5\) (cars per minute) in that order. From outside, \(40\) cars per minute enter at intersection 1 and \(20\) at intersection 2, while \(35\) leave at intersection 3 and \(25\) at intersection 4. Find all flows that satisfy conservation. If street \(4 \to 1\) is closed for repairs and flows cannot be negative, what is the largest flow the diagonal street \(1 \to 3\) may have to carry?

title: Exercise (A1)
content:
State the polynomial interpolation theorem, including its hypotheses. True or false: there is a polynomial \(p \in 
R[x]_{\le 1}\) with \(p(1) = 2\) and \(p(1) = 3\) . Which hypothesis of the theorem fails? In balancing a chemical equation, what does it mean if the null space of the coefficient matrix has dimension \(1\) ? Dimension \(2\) ? Why is lights out modeled over \(
F_2\) and not over \(
R\) ? A connected network has \(6\) vertices and \(9\) edges. What is the rank of its incidence matrix, and how many free parameters does the solution set of a consistent flow problem have?

title: Exercise (B1: Interpolating four points)
content: Find the polynomial \(p \in \nQ[x]_{\le 3}\) with \(p(0) = -1\) , \(p(1) = 1\) , \(p(2) = 3\) and \(p(3) = 11\) . Justify that there is only one.

title: Exercise (B2: Balancing a redox reaction)
content: Potassium permanganate reacts with hydrochloric acid: \[ a\, \mathrm{KMnO_4} + b\, \mathrm{HCl} \longrightarrow c\, \mathrm{KCl} + d\, \mathrm{MnCl_2} + e\, \mathrm{H_2O} + f\, \mathrm{Cl_2} . \] Write the conservation equations for K, Mn, O, H and Cl, find all rational solutions, and hence the balanced equation with the smallest positive integer coefficients.

title: Exercise (B3: A ring road)
content: Four intersections lie on a ring of one-way streets \(1 \to 2\) , \(2 \to 3\) , \(3 \to 4\) , \(4 \to 1\) , with flows \(f_1, f_2, f_3, f_4\) in that order. From outside, \(30\) cars per minute enter at intersection 1 and \(10\) at intersection 3, while \(15\) leave at intersection 2 and \(25\) at intersection 4. Write down the incidence matrix \(\N\) and the supply vector \(\s\) , and explain without computation why the system \(\N\mathbf{f} = \s\) is consistent. Find all solutions. If all flows must be non-negative, what is the smallest possible flow on each street?

title: Exercise (C1: The 2 × 2 puzzle)
content: Consider lights out on a \(2 \times 2\) grid, where pressing a light toggles it and its two horizontal and vertical neighbors. Number the cells \(1 = (1, 1)\) , \(2 = (1, 2)\) , \(3 = (2, 1)\) , \(4 = (2, 2)\) . Write down the matrix \(\A \in M_4(\nF_2)\) of the puzzle. Show that \(\A^2 = \I\) . Deduce that every pattern is solvable by exactly one set of presses, and find the presses that switch off the pattern with only light \(1\) on.

title: Exercise (C2: Interpolating values and slopes)
content: For \(p = c_0 + c_1x + c_2x^2 + c_3x^3 \in F[x]_{\le 3}\) , define its (formal) derivative \(p' = c_1 + 2c_2x + 3c_3x^2\) . Prove that for every field \(F\) and all \(a, b, c, d \in F\) there is exactly one \(p \in F[x]_{\le 3}\) with \[ p(0) = a, \qquad p'(0) = b, \qquad p(1) = c, \qquad p'(1) = d . \] Find this \(p\) over \(\nQ\) for \((a, b, c, d) = (0, 1, 1, 0)\) . Hint: in (a), check that elimination never divides by an element that could be zero in some field.

title: Exercise (C3: Networks in several pieces)
content: Let \(\N \in M_{m \times k}(\nR)\) be the incidence matrix of a network with \(m\) vertices. Say that vertices \(v\) and \(w\) are linked if they are joined by a sequence of vertices in which consecutive ones share an edge, in either direction (every vertex is linked to itself by the sequence of length zero). Show that “linked” is an equivalence relation. Its equivalence classes are called the components of the network; let \(c\) be their number. Prove that \(\rank \N = m - c\) .

title: Lemma 2.7.1 (Factor Theorem for a Linear Divisor)
content: Let \(p \in F[x]\) and \(c \in F\) . Then there is \(q \in F[x]\) such that \[ p = (x - c)\,q + p(c). \] In particular, if \(c\) is a root of \(p\) , then \(p = (x - c)\,q\) .

title: Lemma 2.7.2 (Root bound)
content: Let \(n \in \nN\) , and let \(p \in F[x]\) be non-zero with \(\deg p \le n\) . Then \(p\) has at most \(n\) distinct roots in \(F\) .

title: Proposition 2.7.4 (Rank of an incidence matrix)
content: Let \(\N \in M_{m \times k}(\nR)\) be the incidence matrix of a connected network with \(m\) vertices. Then \(\rank \N = m - 1\) .

title: Theorem 2.7.3 (Polynomial interpolation)
content: Let \(x_0, x_1, \dots, x_n \in F\) be distinct , and let \(y_0, y_1, \dots, y_n \in F\) be arbitrary. Then there is exactly one polynomial \(p \in F[x]_{\le n}\) with \(p(x_i) = y_i\) for \(i = 0, 1, \dots, n\) .

title: Definition 3.1.1 (Linear Map)
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be vector spaces over the same field \(F\) . A function \(T \colon V \to W\) is a linear map (or linear transformation ) over \(F\) if \(T(\u + \v) = T(\u) + T(\v)\) for all \(\u, \v \in V\) , and \(T(c\v) = cT(\v)\) for all \(c \in F\) and all \(\v \in V\) . A linear map \(T \colon V \to V\) from a space to itself is also called a linear operator on \(V\) . We often write \(T\v\) for \(T(\v)\) .

title: Example (A Constant Function)
content: Is \(T \colon \nR \to \nR\) , \(T(x) = 5\) , linear?

title: Example (Maps Given by Formulas in Coordinates)
content: Show that \(T \colon F^3 \to F^2\) , \(T(a_1, a_2, a_3) = (2a_1 + a_3,\ a_2 - a_1)\) , is linear. Let \(\sB = (\v_1, \dots, \v_n)\) be a basis of a vector space \(V\) over \(F\) . Show that the coordinate map \(V \to F^n\) , \(\v \mapsto \coord{\v}{\sB}\) , is linear.

title: Example (Too Many Conditions)
content: Is there a linear map \(T \colon \nR^2 \to \nR^3\) with \[ T(1, 0) = (2, 3, 4), \qquad T(1, 1) = (3, 4, 5), \qquad T(2, 3) = (4, 5, 6)? \]

content:

title: Example (Differentiation)
content: Show that \(D \colon F[x] \to F[x]\) , \(D(p) = p'\) , is linear. Show also that \(D\) maps \(F[x]_{\le n}\) into \(F[x]_{\le n-1}\) for \(n \ge 1\) .

title: Example (Identity Map)
content: The identity \(\id_V \colon V \to V\) , \(\v \mapsto \v\) , is linear: \(\id_V(\u + \v) = \u + \v = \id_V(\u) + \id_V(\v)\) and \(\id_V(c\v) = c\v = c\,\id_V(\v)\) .

title: Example (Inclusion Map)
content: If \(U\) is a subspace of \(V\) , the inclusion \(\iota \colon U \to V\) , \(\iota(\u) = \u\) , is linear, because the operations of \(U\) are those of \(V\) . Its formula is the identity’s, but its codomain is bigger. For instance \(\nR[x]_{\le 2} \to \nR[x]\) is an inclusion.

title: Example (Integration)
content: Show that \(J \colon \nR[x] \to \nR[x]\) , \(J(p)(x) = \int_0^x p(t)\,\dd t\) , is linear.

title: Example (Finding a Formula from Values on a Basis)
content: Show that there is exactly one linear map \(T \colon \nR^2 \to \nR^3\) with \[ T(1, 1) = (1, 2, 0), \qquad T(1, -1) = (3, 0, 2), \] and find \(T(x, y)\) .

title: Example (Composition with a Fixed Function)
content: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be sets and \(g \colon X \to Y\) a function. Show that \(C_g \colon F^Y \to F^X\) , \(C_g(h) = h \circ g\) , is linear. Deduce that \(\nR[x] \to \nR[x]\) , \(p(x) \mapsto p(x + 1)\) , is linear.

title: Example (Multiplication by a Matrix)
content: Let \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) . Show that \(T_\A \colon F^n \to F^m\) , \(T_\A(\x) = \A\x\) , is a linear map.

title: Example (Multiplication by x)
content: Show that \(M \colon F[x] \to F[x]\) , \(M(p) = xp\) , is linear.

title: Example (Length)
content: Is \(T \colon \nR^2 \to \nR\) , \(T(x, y) = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}\) , linear?

title: Example (Projection onto an Axis)
content: Show that \(T \colon \nR^2 \to \nR^2\) , \(T(a_1, a_2) = (a_1, 0)\) , is linear.

content: For any \(V\) and \(W\) over \(F\) , the zero map \(0 \colon V \to W\) , \(\v \mapsto \0_W\) , is linear: \(\0_W = \0_W + \0_W\) and \(\0_W = c\0_W\) ( @thm-scalar-zero-vector ).

title: Theorem 3.1.3 (One-Line Test for Linearity)
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be vector spaces over \(F\) , and let \(T \colon V \to W\) be a function. Then \(T\) is linear if and only if \[ T(c\u + \v) = cT(\u) + T(\v) \qquad \text{for all } c \in F \text{ and all } \u, \v \in V . \]

title: Theorem 3.1.4 (Linear Maps Preserve Linear Combinations)
content: Let \(T \colon V \to W\) be linear, let \(\v_1, \dots, \v_k \in V\) and \(a_1, \dots, a_k \in F\) , where \(k \ge 0\) . Then \[ T(a_1\v_1 + \dots + a_k\v_k) = a_1T(\v_1) + \dots + a_kT(\v_k). \]

title: Theorem 3.1.6 (Linear Maps on an Arbitrary Basis)
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be vector spaces over \(F\) , let \(B\) be a basis of \(V\) (possibly infinite, in the sense of @thm-basis-extension-general ), and for each \(\b \in B\) let \(\w_{\b} \in W\) be any vector. Then there is exactly one linear map \(T \colon V \to W\) with \(T\b = \w_{\b}\) for every \(\b \in B\) .

title: Theorem 3.1.5 (Linear Maps Are Determined by a Basis)
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be vector spaces over \(F\) , let \(\sB = (\v_1, \dots, \v_n)\) be a basis of \(V\) , and let \(\w_1, \dots, \w_n \in W\) be any vectors. Then there exists exactly one linear map \(T \colon V \to W\) such that \[ T(\v_i) = \w_i \qquad \text{for } i = 1, \dots, n . \] It is given by \(T(a_1\v_1 + \dots + a_n\v_n) = a_1\w_1 + \dots + a_n\w_n\) for all \(a_1, \dots, a_n \in F\) .

title: Theorem 3.1.2 (Linear Maps Preserve Negatives)
content: Let \(T \colon V \to W\) be linear. Then \(T(-\v) = -T(\v)\) and \(T(\u - \v) = T(\u) - T(\v)\) for all \(\u, \v \in V\) .

title: Theorem 3.1.1 (Linear Maps Send Zero to Zero)
content: Let \(T \colon V \to W\) be linear. Then \(T(\0_V) = \0_W\) .

title: Definition 3.2.2 (Image)
content: Let \(T \colon V \to W\) be a linear map over \(F\) . The image of \(T\) is the subset of the codomain \[ \im T \coloneqq \{ T(\v) : \v \in V \} = \{ \w \in W : \w = T(\v) \text{ for some } \v \in V \} \subseteq W . \]

title: Definition 3.2.1 (Kernel)
content: Let \(T \colon V \to W\) be a linear map over \(F\) . The kernel of \(T\) is the subset of the domain \[ \ker T \coloneqq \{ \v \in V : T(\v) = \0_W \} \subseteq V . \]

title: Example (Differentiation)
content: Find the kernel and image of \(D \colon \nR[x]_{\le 3} \to \nR[x]_{\le 2}\) , \(D(p) = p'\) .

title: Example (Integration)
content: Find the kernel and image of \(J \colon \nR[x] \to \nR[x]\) , \(J(p)(x) = \int_0^x p(t)\,\dd t\) , of @exm-integration .

title: Example (The Zero Map and the Identity)
content: Find the kernel and image of the zero map \(0 \colon V \to W\) and of the identity \(\id_V \colon V \to V\) .

title: Exercise (C1: Kernels and Images of a Composite)
content: Let \(T \colon U \to V\) and \(S \colon V \to W\) be linear. Prove that \(\ker T \subseteq \ker(ST)\) and \(\im(ST) \subseteq \im S\) . Give an example, with \(U = V = W = \nR^2\) , where \(\ker T \neq \ker(ST)\) . Deduce that if \(ST\) is injective, then \(T\) is injective, and if \(ST\) is surjective, then \(S\) is surjective.

title: Exercise (C2: When Is a Composite Injective?)
content: Let \(T \colon U \to V\) and \(S \colon V \to W\) be linear, and suppose \(T\) is injective. Prove that \(ST\) is injective if and only if \(\ker S \cap \im T = \{\0\}\) , that is, if and only if \(S\) is injective on \(\im T\) . Give an example where \(S\) is not injective but \(ST\) is.

content:
Let \(D \colon

title: Theorem 3.2.4 (The Image Is Spanned by the Images of a Spanning List)
content: Let \(T \colon V \to W\) be linear, and suppose \((\v_1, \dots, \v_k)\) spans \(V\) . Then \[ \im T = \Span\bigl(T(\v_1), \dots, T(\v_k)\bigr). \] In particular, if \(V\) is finite-dimensional, then so is \(\im T\) , even when \(W\) is not.

title: Theorem 3.2.3 (Kernel Test for Injectivity)
content: Let \(T \colon V \to W\) be linear. Then \(T\) is injective if and only if \(\ker T = \{\0\}\) .

title: Theorem 3.2.5 (Injective Maps Preserve Independence, Surjective Maps Preserve Spanning)
content: Let \(T \colon V \to W\) be linear. If \(T\) is injective and \((\v_1, \dots, \v_k)\) is linearly independent in \(V\) , then \((T(\v_1), \dots, T(\v_k))\) is linearly independent in \(W\) . If \(T\) is surjective and \((\v_1, \dots, \v_k)\) spans \(V\) , then \((T(\v_1), \dots, T(\v_k))\) spans \(W\) . If \((\v_1, \dots, \v_n)\) is a basis of \(V\) , then \(T\) is injective if and only if \((T(\v_1), \dots, T(\v_n))\) is linearly independent, and \(T\) is surjective if and only if \((T(\v_1), \dots, T(\v_n))\) spans \(W\) .

title: Theorem 3.2.2 (The Image Is a Subspace)
content: Let \(T \colon V \to W\) be linear. Then: \(\im T\) is a subspace of \(W\) ; \(T\) is surjective if and only if \(\im T = W\) .

title: Theorem 3.2.1 (The Kernel Is a Subspace)
content: Let \(T \colon V \to W\) be linear. Then \(\ker T\) is a subspace of \(V\) .

title: Corollary 3.3.2 (Consequences of Rank–Nullity)
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be finite-dimensional vector spaces over \(F\) , and let \(T \colon V \to W\) be linear. \(T\) is injective if and only if \(\rank T = \dim V\) . \(T\) is surjective if and only if \(\rank T = \dim W\) . If \(\dim V > \dim W\) , then \(T\) is not injective. If \(\dim V < \dim W\) , then \(T\) is not surjective. If \(\dim V = \dim W\) , then \(T\) is injective \(\iff\) \(T\) is surjective \(\iff\) \(T\) is bijective.

title: Definition 3.3.1 (Nullity)
content: Let \(T \colon V \to W\) be a linear map with \(\ker T\) finite-dimensional. The nullity of \(T\) is \(\nullity T \coloneqq \dim \ker T\) .

title: Definition 3.3.2 (Rank)
content: Let \(T \colon V \to W\) be a linear map with \(\im T\) finite-dimensional. The rank of \(T\) is \(\rank T \coloneqq \dim \im T\) .

title: Example (Dimension of a Kernel from a Surjective Map)
content: Find the dimension of each subspace. The trace-free matrices \(U = \{ \A \in M_n(F) : \tr \A = 0 \}\) ( @exm-trace-free-matrices ). \(U' = \{ p \in \nR[x]_{\le n} : \int_0^1 p(t)\,\dd t = 0 \}\) .

title: Example (Prescribing Values and Slopes)
content: Show that for all \(a, b, c, d \in \nR\) there is exactly one \(p \in \nR[x]_{\le 3}\) with \[ p(0) = a, \qquad p(1) = b, \qquad p'(0) = c, \qquad p'(1) = d . \] Hence find the cubic that rises from \(0\) at \(x = 0\) to \(1\) at \(x = 1\) with slope \(0\) at both ends.

title: Example (Interpolation as a Count)
content: Let \(x_0, \dots, x_n \in F\) be distinct, and define \(E \colon F[x]_{\le n} \to F^{n+1}\) by \(E(p) = \bigl(p(x_0), \dots, p(x_n)\bigr)\) . Show that \(E\) is bijective, and deduce @thm-interpolation-unique .

title: Exercise (C1: A Lower Bound for the Rank of a Composite)
content: Let \(U\) and \(V\) be finite-dimensional, let \(W\) be a vector space, all over \(F\) , and let \(T \colon U \to V\) and \(S \colon V \to W\) be linear. Write \(ST\) for the composite \(S \circ T\) , which is linear (see the note before @exr-kernel-image-c1 ). Let \(S' \colon \im T \to W\) be the restriction of \(S\) to \(\im T\) , that is, \(S'(\v) = S(\v)\) for \(\v \in \im T\) . Show that \(S'\) is linear, that \(\im S' = \im(ST)\) and that \(\ker S' = \ker S \cap \im T\) . Deduce that \(\rank(ST) = \rank T - \dim(\ker S \cap \im T)\) . Hence prove Sylvester’s inequality : \(\rank(ST) \ge \rank S + \rank T - \dim V\) . Deduce that \(\rank(\A\B) \ge \rank \A + \rank \B - n\) for \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) and \(\B \in M_{n \times p}(F)\) . Hint: for (c), compare \(\ker S \cap \im T\) with \(\ker S\) .

title: Theorem 3.3.1 (Rank–Nullity Theorem)
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space, let \(W\) be any vector space over the same field, and let \(T \colon V \to W\) be linear. Then \(\ker T\) and \(\im T\) are finite-dimensional, and \[ \nullity T + \rank T = \dim V . \]

title: Definition 3.4.2 (Powers and Polynomials of an Operator)
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) and \(T \in \cL(V)\) . The powers of \(T\) are defined recursively by \[ T^0 \coloneqq \id_V, \qquad T^{k+1} \coloneqq T^k T \quad (k \in \nN). \] For \(p = a_0 + a_1x + \dots + a_Nx^N \in F[x]\) , the operator \(p(T) \in \cL(V)\) is \[ p(T) \coloneqq a_0\id_V + a_1T + a_2T^2 + \dots + a_NT^N . \]

title: Definition 3.4.1 (The space of linear maps)
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be vector spaces over the same field \(F\) . We write \(\cL(V, W)\) for the set of all linear maps \(V \to W\) , and \(\cL(V) \coloneqq \cL(V, V)\) for the set of linear operators on \(V\) ( @def-linear-transformation ). For \(S, T \in \cL(V, W)\) and \(c \in F\) , the sum \(S + T\) and the scalar multiple \(cT\) are the functions \(V \to W\) defined by \[ (S + T)(\v) \coloneqq S\v + T\v, \qquad (cT)(\v) \coloneqq c\,(T\v) \qquad \text{for every } \v \in V . \]

title: Example (Differentiation Is Nilpotent)
content: Let \(n \ge 0\) and let \(D \in \cL(F[x]_{\le n})\) be (formal) differentiation ( @exm-differentiation ), \(D(a_0 + a_1x + \dots + a_nx^n) = a_1 + 2a_2x + \dots + na_nx^{n-1}\) , where \(ka_k\) means \(a_k\) added to itself \(k\) times. Show that \(D^{n+1} = 0\) . Show also that \(D^n \neq 0\) when \(F = \nR\) .

title: Example (Operators That Satisfy a Polynomial)
content: With \(P\) and \(R\) as in @exm-rotation-projection-dont-commute , find non-zero polynomials \(p\) and \(q\) with \(p(P) = 0\) and \(q(R) = 0\) . Also, for an arbitrary \(p \in F[x]\) , compute \(p(\id_V)\) and \(p(Z)\) , where \(Z \in \cL(V)\) is the zero operator.

content: For \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) , write \(T_\A \colon F^n \to F^m\) , \(\x \mapsto \A\x\) , for the matrix map of @exm-matrix-transformation . title: Exercise (B1: Computing compositions)
content: Let \(S, T \in \cL(\nR^2)\) be given by \(S(x, y) = (x + y, \, y)\) and \(T(x, y) = (y, \, x)\) . Compute \(ST\) , \(TS\) and \(2S - T\) . Compute \(S^2\) and \(S^k\) for every \(k \in \nN\) . Hence show that \((S - \id)^2 = 0\) .

title: Exercise (B2: Operators that preserve a subspace)
content: Let \(U\) be a subspace of \(V\) , and let \[ \mathcal{A}_U \coloneqq \{ T \in \cL(V) : T\u \in U \text{ for every } \u \in U \} . \] Prove that \(\mathcal{A}_U\) is a subspace of \(\cL(V)\) , that \(\id_V \in \mathcal{A}_U\) , and that \(ST \in \mathcal{A}_U\) whenever \(S, T \in \mathcal{A}_U\) .

title: Exercise (B3: A polynomial that kills D)
content: Let \(D \in \cL(\nR[x]_{\le 2})\) be differentiation. Find a non-zero polynomial \(p\) with \(p(D) = 0\) . Show that no non-zero polynomial \(q\) of degree at most \(2\) satisfies \(q(D) = 0\) . Hence, or otherwise, compute \((\id + D)^3\) as a combination of \(\id, D, D^2\) , and evaluate \((\id + D)^3(x^2)\) .

title: Exercise (C1: The Heisenberg relation)
content: Let \(F\) be a field, let \(D \in \cL(F[x])\) be formal differentiation, \(D(\sum_k a_kx^k) = \sum_{k \ge 1} ka_kx^{k-1}\) ( @exm-differentiation ), and let \(S \in \cL(F[x])\) be multiplication by \(x\) , \(S(p) = xp\) (the map \(M\) of @exm-multiplication-by-x ). Prove that \(DS - SD = \id\) . Let \(T \in \cL(F^n, F^m)\) . Prove that \(T = T_\A\) , where \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) is the matrix with columns \(T\e_1, \dots, T\e_n\) . Now suppose that \(F\) has characteristic \(0\) ( @def-characteristic ), and let \(n \ge 1\) . Deduce that there are no operators \(D', S' \in \cL(F^n)\) with \(D'S' - S'D' = \id\) . Show that the assumption on the characteristic in (c) cannot be dropped. Hint: for (c), use (b) and consider traces.

title: Exercise (C2: Commuting nilpotent operators)
content: Let \(S, T \in \cL(V)\) . Suppose \(ST = TS\) . Prove that \((S + T)^n = \sum_{k=0}^{n} \binom{n}{k} S^kT^{n-k}\) for every \(n \in \nN\) , where \(\binom{n}{k} S^kT^{n-k}\) means \(S^kT^{n-k}\) added to itself \(\binom{n}{k}\) times. Deduce that if \(ST = TS\) , \(S^a = 0\) and \(T^b = 0\) for some \(a, b \ge 1\) , then \((S + T)^{a+b-1} = 0\) . Show that (b) fails without \(ST = TS\) : give nilpotent \(S, T \in \cL(\nR^2)\) such that \(S + T\) is not nilpotent. Hint: for (c), try maps that send one standard basis vector to the other and the other to \(\0\) .

title: Theorem 3.4.2 (Composition of Linear Maps)
content: Let \(U, V, W, X\) be vector spaces over \(F\) . (Linearity) If \(T \in \cL(U, V)\) and \(S \in \cL(V, W)\) , then \(ST \in \cL(U, W)\) . (Associativity) If \(T \in \cL(U, V)\) , \(S \in \cL(V, W)\) and \(R \in \cL(W, X)\) , then \(R(ST) = (RS)T\) . (Identities) If \(T \in \cL(U, V)\) , then \(T\id_U = T = \id_V T\) . (Distributivity) If \(T, T_1, T_2 \in \cL(U, V)\) , \(S, S_1, S_2 \in \cL(V, W)\) and \(c \in F\) , then \[ \begin{aligned} (S_1 + S_2)T &= S_1T + S_2T, \\ S(T_1 + T_2) &= ST_1 + ST_2, \\ (cS)T &= c(ST) = S(cT). \end{aligned} \]

title: Theorem 3.4.1 (\cL(V, W) Is a Vector Space)
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be vector spaces over \(F\) . If \(S, T \in \cL(V, W)\) and \(c \in F\) , then \(S + T\) and \(cT\) are linear. With the operations of @def-space-of-linear-maps , \(\cL(V, W)\) is a vector space over \(F\) . Its zero vector is the zero map \(\v \mapsto \0_W\) , and the negative of \(T\) is \((-1)T \colon \v \mapsto -T\v\) .

title: Theorem 3.4.3 (Polynomials in One Operator)
content: Let \(T \in \cL(V)\) and \(p, q \in F[x]\) . Then: \(T^jT^k = T^{j+k}\) for all \(j, k \in \nN\) ; \((p + q)(T) = p(T) + q(T)\) and \((pq)(T) = p(T)\,q(T)\) ; \(p(T)\,q(T) = q(T)\,p(T)\) .

title: Corollary 3.5.5 (The Coordinate Isomorphism)
content: Let \(\sB = (\v_1, \dots, \v_n)\) be a basis of a vector space \(V\) over \(F\) . Then the coordinate map \[ V \to F^n, \qquad \v \mapsto \coord{\v}{\sB} \] is an isomorphism, with inverse \((a_1, \dots, a_n) \mapsto a_1\v_1 + \dots + a_n\v_n\) . In particular, every \(n\) -dimensional vector space over \(F\) is isomorphic to \(F^n\) .

title: Definition 3.5.1 (Invertible Linear Map)
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be vector spaces over \(F\) , and let \(T \in \cL(V, W)\) . Then \(T\) is invertible if there exists a linear map \(S \in \cL(W, V)\) such that \[ ST = \id_V \qquad \textbf{and} \qquad TS = \id_W . \]

title: Definition 3.5.3 (Isomorphic Spaces)
content: Vector spaces \(V\) and \(W\) over \(F\) are isomorphic , written \(V \cong W\) , if there exists an isomorphism \(V \to W\) .

title: Definition 3.5.2 (Isomorphism)
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be vector spaces over the same field \(F\) . An isomorphism from \(V\) to \(W\) is an invertible linear map \(T \in \cL(V, W)\) ; equivalently, by @thm-inverse-is-linear , a bijective linear map.

title: Example (One Equation Is Not Enough)
content: On \(\nR[x]\) , let \(D\) be differentiation and \(J(p) \coloneqq \int_0^x p(t)\,\dd t\) , so that \(J(x^k) = \frac{x^{k+1}}{k+1}\) ( @exm-differentiation , @exm-integration ). On the sequence space \(F^{\nN}\) , let \(L(a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots) \coloneqq (a_1, a_2, a_3, \dots)\) and \(R(a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots) \coloneqq (0, a_0, a_1, \dots)\) be the left and right shifts of @exm-shift . title: Theorem 3.5.1 (The Inverse of a Linear Bijection Is Linear)
content: Let \(T \in \cL(V, W)\) be bijective. Then its inverse function \(T^{-1} \colon W \to V\) is linear. Consequently, a linear map \(T\) is invertible if and only if it is bijective.

title: Theorem 3.5.7 (Invertible Operator Theorem)
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space over \(F\) , and let \(T \in \cL(V)\) . The following are equivalent. \(T\) is invertible. \(T\) is injective. \(\ker T = \{\0\}\) , that is, \(\nullity T = 0\) . \(T\) is surjective. \(\rank T = \dim V\) . There is \(S \in \cL(V)\) with \(ST = \id_V\) . There is \(S \in \cL(V)\) with \(TS = \id_V\) . \(T\) maps some basis of \(V\) to a basis of \(V\) . \(T\) maps every basis of \(V\) to a basis of \(V\) .

title: Theorem 3.5.3 (Isomorphism Is an Equivalence Relation)
content: For vector spaces over \(F\) : \(V \cong V\) ; if \(V \cong W\) then \(W \cong V\) ; and if \(U \cong V\) and \(V \cong W\) then \(U \cong W\) .

title: Theorem 3.5.4 (Classification of Finite-Dimensional Spaces)
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be finite-dimensional vector spaces over the same field \(F\) . Then \[ V \cong W \quad \iff \quad \dim V = \dim W . \]

title: Theorem 3.5.2 (Isomorphisms Carry Bases to Bases)
content: Let \(T \colon V \to W\) be an isomorphism, and let \((\v_1, \dots, \v_n)\) be a basis of \(V\) . Then \((T\v_1, \dots, T\v_n)\) is a basis of \(W\) .

title: Theorem 3.5.6 (One-Sided Inverses of Linear Maps)
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be finite-dimensional vector spaces over \(F\) with \(\dim V = \dim W\) . Let \(T \in \cL(V, W)\) and \(S \in \cL(W, V)\) . If \(ST = \id_V\) , then \(TS = \id_W\) . In that case \(T\) and \(S\) are both isomorphisms, \(S = T^{-1}\) and \(T = S^{-1}\) .

title: Corollary 3.6.3 (Matrices of Powers and Polynomials)
page: 3.6 The Matrix of a Linear Map
content: Let \(\sB = (\v_1, \dots, \v_n)\) be a basis of a finite-dimensional space \(V\) , let \(T, S \in \cL(V)\) , \(c \in F\) and \(p \in F[x]\) . Then \([ST]_{\sB} = [S]_{\sB}[T]_{\sB}\) , \([S + T]_{\sB} = [S]_{\sB} + [T]_{\sB}\) , \([cT]_{\sB} = c[T]_{\sB}\) , \([T^k]_{\sB} = ([T]_{\sB})^k\) for \(k \in \nN\) , and \[ [p(T)]_{\sB} = p\bigl([T]_{\sB}\bigr). \]

title: Definition 3.6.1 (Matrix of a Linear Map)
page: 3.6 The Matrix of a Linear Map
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be finite-dimensional vector spaces over \(F\) , with ordered bases \(\sB = (\v_1, \dots, \v_n)\) of \(V\) and \(\sC = (\w_1, \dots, \w_m)\) of \(W\) , and let \(T \in \cL(V, W)\) . The matrix of \(T\) with respect to \(\sB\) and \(\sC\) is the \(m \times n\) matrix \[ \mtx{T}{\sB}{\sC} \coloneqq \begin{pmatrix} \coord{T\v_1}{\sC} & \coord{T\v_2}{\sC} & \cdots & \coord{T\v_n}{\sC} \end{pmatrix} \in M_{m \times n}(F), \] whose \(j\) -th column is the coordinate vector of \(T\v_j\) with respect to \(\sC\) . Equivalently, its entries \(a_{ij}\) are the unique scalars with \[ T\v_j = a_{1j}\w_1 + a_{2j}\w_2 + \dots + a_{mj}\w_m \qquad (j = 1, \dots, n). \] When \(V = W\) and \(\sB = \sC\) , we write \([T]_{\sB} \coloneqq \mtx{T}{\sB}{\sB}\) and call it the matrix of the operator \(T\) with respect to \(\sB\) .

title: Theorem 3.6.4 (\cL(V, W) \cong M_{m \times n}(F))
page: 3.6 The Matrix of a Linear Map
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be finite-dimensional vector spaces over \(F\) with ordered bases \(\sB = (\v_1, \dots, \v_n)\) and \(\sC = (\w_1, \dots, \w_m)\) . Then the map \[ \Phi \colon \cL(V, W) \to M_{m \times n}(F), \qquad T \mapsto \mtx{T}{\sB}{\sC}, \] is an isomorphism. In particular, \(\dim \cL(V, W) = mn = (\dim V)(\dim W)\) .

title: Theorem 3.6.2 (Matrix of a Composition)
page: 3.6 The Matrix of a Linear Map
content: Let \(U, V, W\) be finite-dimensional vector spaces over \(F\) with ordered bases \(\sB\) , \(\sC\) , \(\sD\) respectively. Let \(T \in \cL(U, V)\) and \(S \in \cL(V, W)\) . Then \[ \mtx{ST}{\sB}{\sD} = \mtx{S}{\sC}{\sD}\,\mtx{T}{\sB}{\sC} . \]

title: Theorem 3.6.1 (Coordinates of an Image)
page: 3.6 The Matrix of a Linear Map
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be finite-dimensional vector spaces over \(F\) with ordered bases \(\sB = (\v_1, \dots, \v_n)\) and \(\sC = (\w_1, \dots, \w_m)\) , and let \(T \in \cL(V, W)\) . Then for every \(\v \in V\) , \[ \coord{T\v}{\sC} = \mtx{T}{\sB}{\sC}\,\coord{\v}{\sB} . \] Moreover, \(\mtx{T}{\sB}{\sC}\) is the only matrix \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) with \(\coord{T\v}{\sC} = \A\coord{\v}{\sB}\) for all \(\v \in V\) .

title: Theorem 3.6.5 (Rank and Invertibility from the Matrix)
page: 3.6 The Matrix of a Linear Map
content:
Let \(V\) and \(W\) be finite-dimensional vector spaces over \(F\) with ordered bases \(\sB\) and \(\sC\) , let \(T \in \cL(V, W)\) , and let \(\A = \mtx{T}{\sB}{\sC}\) . The coordinate map \(\v \mapsto \coord{\v}{\sB}\) restricts to an isomorphism \(\ker T 	o 
ul(\A)\) , and the coordinate map \(\w \mapsto \coord{\w}{\sC}\) restricts to an isomorphism \(\im T 	o \col(\A)\) . Hence \[ ank T = ank \A \qquad 	ext{and} \qquad 
ullity T = 
ullity \A . \] Suppose \(\dim V = \dim W\) . Then \(T\) is invertible if and only if \(\A\) is invertible, and in that case \(\mtx{T^{-1}}{\sC}{\sB} = \A^{-1}\) .

title: Definition 3.7.1 (Change-of-coordinates matrix)
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space over \(F\) , and let \(\sB = (\v_1, \dots, \v_n)\) and \(\sC\) be ordered bases of \(V\) . The change-of-coordinates matrix from \(\sB\) to \(\sC\) is the \(n \times n\) matrix \[ \mtx{\id}{\sB}{\sC} \coloneqq \mtx{\id_V}{\sB}{\sC}, \] the matrix of the identity map \(\id_V \colon V \to V\) with respect to the input basis \(\sB\) and the output basis \(\sC\) . Its \(j\) -th column is \(\coord{\v_j}{\sC}\) .

title: Definition 3.7.2 (Similar matrices)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) . We say \(\A\) is similar to \(\B\) , written \(\A \sim \B\) , if there exists an invertible matrix \(\P \in M_n(F)\) such that \[ \B = \P^{-1}\A\P . \]

title: Proposition 3.7.2 (Invertible matrices are changes of basis)
content: Let \(\sB = (\v_1, \dots, \v_n)\) be a basis of \(V\) , and let \(\P = (p_{ij}) \in M_n(F)\) be invertible. Put \[ \v_j' \coloneqq p_{1j}\v_1 + p_{2j}\v_2 + \dots + p_{nj}\v_n \qquad (j = 1, \dots, n). \] Then \(\sB' = (\v_1', \dots, \v_n')\) is a basis of \(V\) , and \(\mtx{\id}{\sB'}{\sB} = \P\) .

title: Proposition 3.7.6 (More similarity invariants)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) with \(\B = \P^{-1}\A\P\) for an invertible \(\P\) . \(\rank \A = \rank \B\) . \(\A\) is invertible if and only if \(\B\) is invertible. For every polynomial \(p \in F[x]\) , \(p(\B) = \P^{-1}p(\A)\P\) . In particular, \(p(\A) = 0\) if and only if \(p(\B) = 0\) ; for example, \(\A^2 = 0\) if and only if \(\B^2 = 0\) .

title: Theorem 3.7.3 (Change of Basis for Linear Maps)
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be finite-dimensional vector spaces over \(F\) , let \(\sB, \sB'\) be bases of \(V\) and \(\sC, \sC'\) bases of \(W\) , and let \(T \colon V \to W\) be linear. Then \[ \mtx{T}{\sB'}{\sC'} = \mtx{\id}{\sC}{\sC'}\,\mtx{T}{\sB}{\sC}\,\mtx{\id}{\sB'}{\sB}. \] In particular, for an operator \(T \in \cL(V)\) and bases \(\sB, \sB'\) of \(V\) , with \(\P = \mtx{\id}{\sB'}{\sB}\) , \[ [T]_{\sB'} = \P^{-1}\,[T]_{\sB}\,\P . \]

title: Theorem 3.7.1 (Change of Coordinates)
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space of dimension \(n\) , and let \(\sB\) , \(\sC\) , \(\sD\) be bases of \(V\) . For every \(\v \in V\) , \(\coord{\v}{\sC} = \mtx{\id}{\sB}{\sC}\coord{\v}{\sB}\) . Moreover, \(\mtx{\id}{\sB}{\sC}\) is the only matrix \(M \in M_n(F)\) with \(\coord{\v}{\sC} = M\coord{\v}{\sB}\) for every \(\v \in V\) . \(\mtx{\id}{\sB}{\sD} = \mtx{\id}{\sC}{\sD}\mtx{\id}{\sB}{\sC}\) . \(\mtx{\id}{\sB}{\sC}\) is invertible, and \(\big(\mtx{\id}{\sB}{\sC}\big)^{-1} = \mtx{\id}{\sC}{\sB}\) .

title: Theorem 3.7.4 (Similar Matrices Represent the Same Operator)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) . If \(V\) is a vector space of dimension \(n\) , \(T \in \cL(V)\) , and \(\sB, \sC\) are bases of \(V\) , then \([T]_{\sB} \sim [T]_{\sC}\) . Conversely, suppose \(\A \sim \B\) . Let \(V\) be any vector space of dimension \(n\) with a basis \(\sB\) , and let \(T \in \cL(V)\) be an operator with \([T]_{\sB} = \A\) . Then there is a basis \(\sC\) of \(V\) with \([T]_{\sC} = \B\) . Such an operator \(T\) in (b) always exists. In particular, \(\A \sim \B\) if and only if \(\A\) and \(\B\) are the matrices of the operator \(\x \mapsto \A\x\) on \(F^n\) in the standard basis and in some basis of \(F^n\) , respectively.

title: Theorem 3.7.5 (Trace Is a Similarity Invariant)
content: If \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) are similar, then \(\tr \A = \tr \B\) .

title: Definition 3.8.1 (Equivalent matrices)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) . We say \(\A\) is equivalent to \(\B\) if there exist invertible matrices \(\Q \in M_m(F)\) and \(\P \in M_n(F)\) such that \[ \B = \Q\A\P . \]

title: Example (A column–row factorization)
content: Find the column–row factorization of \(\A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 0 & 3 \\ 2 & 4 & 1 & 4 \\ 3 & 6 & 1 & 7 \end{pmatrix} \in M_{3 \times 4}(\nR)\) .

content: Define what it means for \(\A, \B \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) to be equivalent. State the Rank Normal Form theorem for a matrix \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) . title: Exercise (B3: Rank-one pieces)
content: Let \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) . Use @thm-column-row-factorization to show that if \(\rank \A = 1\) , then \(\A = \x\y\tp\) for some non-zero \(\x \in F^m\) and \(\y \in F^n\) . Show that if \(\rank \A = r \ge 1\) , then \(\A\) is a sum of \(r\) matrices of rank \(1\) , and that it is not a sum of fewer than \(r\) matrices of rank \(1\) . Write \(\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 0 & 3 \\ 2 & 4 & 1 & 4 \\ 3 & 6 & 1 & 7 \end{pmatrix}\) as a sum of two rank-one matrices.

title: Exercise (C1: Frobenius’s rank inequality)
content: Let \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) , \(\B \in M_{n \times p}(F)\) and \(\C \in M_{p \times q}(F)\) . Write \(N = \nul(\A) \subseteq F^n\) , and let \(S \colon F^n \to F^m\) be \(S\y = \A\y\) . Show that \(\col(\A\B) = \{ \A\y : \y \in \col(\B) \}\) , and deduce from Rank–Nullity for \(S|_{\col(\B)}\) that \(\rank(\A\B) = \rank \B - \dim(N \cap \col(\B))\) . Show similarly that \(\rank(\A\B\C) = \rank(\B\C) - \dim(N \cap \col(\B\C))\) . Prove that \(\col(\B\C) \subseteq \col(\B)\) , and deduce Frobenius’s inequality \[ \rank(\A\B\C) + \rank \B \ge \rank(\A\B) + \rank(\B\C). \] Deduce Sylvester’s inequality for matrices from (c). Hint: for (d), look for a special choice of the middle factor.

content:
